#### Course 10.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Computer Architecture and Accelerators approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Computer Architecture and Accelerators system implementing Computer Architecture and Accelerators - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 10.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 11.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Compilers and Programming Language Theory approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Compilers and Programming Language Theory system implementing Compilers and Programming Language Theory - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.042J Mathematics for Computer Science principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 11.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

## Program 12: Theory of Computation and Complexity

**Program Description:** Advanced program in Theory of Computation and Complexity covering foundational theory, implementation from scratch, research-level understanding suitable for doctoral studies at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech.

**Prerequisites:** Linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, algorithms, programming proficiency. Programs followed in numerical order.

**Selected Bibliography:**

- Introduction to Algorithms - Cormen et al. - MIT Press - Why: Definitive algorithms with formal proofs - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal analysis beyond lectures - Used With: All algorithm chapters
- Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective - Bryant - Why: Systems performance for AI - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Memory hierarchy and optimization
- Deep Learning - Goodfellow et al. - MIT Press - Why: Mathematical foundations - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal derivations

#### Course 12.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Theory of Computation and Complexity approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Theory of Computation and Complexity system implementing Theory of Computation and Complexity - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.042J Mathematics for Computer Science principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 12.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 13.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Discrete Mathematics and Graph Theory approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Discrete Mathematics and Graph Theory system implementing Vector Spaces and Linear Transformations using 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 13.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

## Program 14: Optimization Theory

**Program Description:** Advanced program in Optimization Theory covering foundational theory, implementation from scratch, research-level understanding suitable for doctoral studies at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech.

**Prerequisites:** Linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, algorithms, programming proficiency. Programs followed in numerical order.

- Introduction to Algorithms - Cormen et al. - MIT Press - Why: Definitive algorithms with formal proofs - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal analysis beyond lectures - Used With: All algorithm chapters

#### Course 15.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Information Theory and Coding Theory approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Information Theory and Coding Theory system implementing Information Theory and Coding Theory - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.042J Mathematics for Computer Science principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 15.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 16.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Partial Differential Equations and Scientific Machine Learning approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Partial Differential Equations and Scientific Machine Learning system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 18.06 Linear Algebra principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 16.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

**Research Question:** Can we build Stochastic Calculus and Diffusion Models system implementing Stochastic Calculus and Diffusion Models - Formal Foundations 1 using 18.06 Linear Algebra principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

#### Course 18.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Deep Learning approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Deep Learning system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.036 Introduction to Machine Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 19.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Computer Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Computer Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models system implementing Computer Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models - Formal Foundations 1 using CS231N Deep Learning for Computer Vision principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs

- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis

#### Course 19.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Computer Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Computer Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models system implementing Computer Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models - Formal Foundations 1 using CS230 Deep Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 19.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

## Program 20: Natural Language Processing

**Program Description:** Advanced program in Natural Language Processing covering foundational theory, implementation from scratch, research-level understanding suitable for doctoral studies at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech.

**Prerequisites:** Linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, algorithms, programming proficiency. Programs followed in numerical order.

- Introduction to Algorithms - Cormen et al. - MIT Press - Why: Definitive algorithms with formal proofs - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal analysis beyond lectures - Used With: All algorithm chapters

- Deep Learning - Goodfellow et al. - MIT Press - Why: Mathematical foundations - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal derivations

#### Course 21.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Generative AI and Large Language Models approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Generative AI and Large Language Models system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using CS230 Deep Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

- Introduction to Algorithms - Cormen et al. - MIT Press - Why: Definitive algorithms with formal proofs - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal analysis beyond lectures - Used With: All algorithm chapters
- Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective - Bryant - Why: Systems performance for AI - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Memory hierarchy and optimization

#### Course 22.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning system implementing Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.036 Introduction to Machine Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 22.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 22.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning system implementing Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 22.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions

## Program 23: Bayesian Machine Learning

**Program Description:** Advanced program in Bayesian Machine Learning covering foundational theory, implementation from scratch, research-level understanding suitable for doctoral studies at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech.

**Prerequisites:** Linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, algorithms, programming proficiency. Programs followed in numerical order.

**Selected Bibliography:**

- Introduction to Algorithms - Cormen et al. - MIT Press - Why: Definitive algorithms with formal proofs - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal analysis beyond lectures - Used With: All algorithm chapters

- Deep Learning - Goodfellow et al. - MIT Press - Why: Mathematical foundations - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal derivations

#### Course 23.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Bayesian Machine Learning approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Bayesian Machine Learning system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.867 Machine Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

#### Course 24.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Causal Inference and Causal AI approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Causal Inference and Causal AI system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.036 Introduction to Machine Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 24.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 24.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Causal Inference and Causal AI approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Causal Inference and Causal AI system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.867 Machine Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 25.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Cryptography and Secure AI Systems approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Cryptography and Secure AI Systems system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 25.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 26.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Computational Neuroscience and Brain-Inspired AI approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Computational Neuroscience and Brain-Inspired AI system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

#### Course 27.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Numerical Methods and Scientific Computing approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Numerical Methods and Scientific Computing system implementing Vector Spaces and Linear Transformations using 18.06 Linear Algebra principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 27.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 27.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Numerical Methods and Scientific Computing approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Numerical Methods and Scientific Computing system implementing Vector Spaces and Linear Transformations using 18.01SC Single Variable Calculus principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 28.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Formal Verification and AI Safety Verification approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Formal Verification and AI Safety Verification system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 28.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

## Program 29: High-Performance Computing and AI Systems

**Program Description:** Advanced program in High-Performance Computing and AI Systems covering foundational theory, implementation from scratch, research-level understanding suitable for doctoral studies at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech.

**Prerequisites:** Linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, algorithms, programming proficiency. Programs followed in numerical order.

- Introduction to Algorithms - Cormen et al. - MIT Press - Why: Definitive algorithms with formal proofs - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal analysis beyond lectures - Used With: All algorithm chapters

- Deep Learning - Goodfellow et al. - MIT Press - Why: Mathematical foundations - Difficulty: Advanced - Adds: Formal derivations

#### Course 29.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing High-Performance Computing and AI Systems approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build High-Performance Computing and AI Systems system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.046J Design and Analysis of Algorithms principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 29.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

**Research Question:** Can we build Game Theory, Mechanism Design, and Multi-Agent Systems system implementing Game Theory, Mechanism Design, and Multi-Agent Systems - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.042J Mathematics for Computer Science principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

#### Course 30.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Game Theory, Mechanism Design, and Multi-Agent Systems approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Game Theory, Mechanism Design, and Multi-Agent Systems system implementing Game Theory, Mechanism Design, and Multi-Agent Systems - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 30.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs

- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis

#### Course 31.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Computational Linguistics and Arabic Natural Language Processing approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Computational Linguistics and Arabic Natural Language Processing system implementing Computational Linguistics and Arabic Natural Language Processing - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 32.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Robotics, Control Theory, and Embodied Intelligence approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Robotics, Control Theory, and Embodied Intelligence system implementing Robotics, Control Theory, and Embodied Intelligence - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 33.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Cognitive Science and Decision Making approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Cognitive Science and Decision Making system implementing Cognitive Science and Decision Making - Formal Foundations 1 using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 33.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 34.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Complex Systems, Chaos, and Emergence approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Complex Systems, Chaos, and Emergence system implementing Complex Systems, Chaos, and Emergence - Formal Foundations 1 using 18.01SC Single Variable Calculus principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 34.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs

- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis

#### Course 35.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing AI Safety, Alignment, and Interpretability approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build AI Safety, Alignment, and Interpretability system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.034 Artificial Intelligence principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs

- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis

#### Course 36.2 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing Data Engineering and Data-Centric AI for Foundation Models approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build Data Engineering and Data-Centric AI for Foundation Models system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.046J Design and Analysis of Algorithms principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 36.2 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

#### Course 38.1 Final Research Project

**Problem:** Existing AI Systems Engineering, MLOps, LLMOps, and Evaluation approaches lack from-scratch implementation with formal correctness and performance analysis under realistic constraints required for AI company moat.

**Research Question:** Can we build AI Systems Engineering, MLOps, LLMOps, and Evaluation system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research

#### Course 38.1 Completion Checklist

- [ ] Theory mastered - Explain formal definitions, theorems, proofs
- [ ] Problem sets solved with 90%+ accuracy
- [ ] From-scratch implementation completed with correctness and benchmarking
- [ ] Laboratory executed with measurements and analysis
- [ ] Research project completed and compared to baselines
- [ ] Documentation with proofs and design decisions
- [ ] Mastery demonstrated via teaching and unfamiliar application

**Research Question:** Can we build AI Systems Engineering, MLOps, LLMOps, and Evaluation system implementing Supervised Learning Theory and Risk Minimization using CS229 Machine Learning principles under constraint Z (memory, distributed, adversarial) differently from library-based approaches?

**Hypothesis:** From-scratch implementation with formal invariants will achieve competitive performance within 20% of optimized libraries while providing deeper understanding.

**Technical Approach:** Literature review -> Formal specification -> From-scratch implementation -> Testing -> Benchmarking -> Analysis

**From-Scratch Components:** Core data structures, algorithms, memory management, concurrency - independently implemented

**Experimental Methodology:** Controlled experiments, fixed seeds, repeated trials, statistical significance, profiling

**Baselines:** Standard library implementations, textbook algorithms, published results

**Metrics:** Correctness, complexity, performance (latency, throughput, memory), code quality

**Expected Contribution:** Research-grade system suitable for PhD portfolio at MIT, Stanford, CMU, Berkeley, Georgia Tech and foundation for AI company technology

**GitHub Deliverables:** README.md, src/, docs/, tests/, benchmarks/, papers/

**Research Extension:** Paper, Open Source, Startup Technology, Deeper Research
